r4a-split-not-snap.title: Split-not-snap (THE #1 check)
r4a-split-not-snap.imperative: Verify TestSplitNotSnap genuinely proves a straddling segment SPLITS into two SAME-class pieces at the EXACT line distance -- quote the assertion. Confirm no existing boundary moved and _split_at_lines never snaps to a nearby boundary. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4a-split-not-snap.finding: CONFIRMED, THE #1 check. Code (_split_at_lines): np.searchsorted locates the insertion index; if the line is not already a boundary (within _EPS_M=1e-9), it does 'straddled_type = types[idx - 1]; boundaries.insert(idx, line); types.insert(idx, straddled_type)' -- inserts the EXACT line distance as a new boundary and duplicates the STRADDLED segment's own type onto both resulting pieces; it never touches boundaries[idx-1] or boundaries[idx] (the flanking pre-existing boundaries), so no existing boundary is ever moved. Test proof, quoted (test_straddling_corner_splits_into_two_corner_pieces_at_exact_distance): fixture has segment [200,400) typed CORNER; line=350.0 straddles it, with pre-existing boundaries 150m/50m away (deliberately far, so a snap would be visibly wrong per the test's own comment). Assertions: 'assert line in b2.tolist()' (exact distance present), 'assert t2[idx - 1] == CORNER' and 'assert t2[idx] == CORNER' (BOTH flanking pieces keep the straddled segment's OWN class, not re-typed), then 'assert 200.0 in b2.tolist()' and 'assert 400.0 in b2.tolist()' (the pre-existing boundaries are UNPERTURBED -- proves no snap, not just proves insertion). A sibling test (test_straddling_straight_splits_into_two_straight_pieces) repeats the pattern for STRAIGHT. A third test (test_line_exactly_on_existing_boundary_is_not_duplicated) proves the idempotent case: a line already coinciding with a boundary is not duplicated ('assert b2.tolist().count(400.0) == 1'). Reproduced independently (17/17 green, this class's 3 tests included). Genuinely proves split-not-snap, not a coincidental pass.

r4b-sliver-merge-exempt.title: Sliver-merge EXEMPTS sector cuts (both directions tested)
r4b-sliver-merge-exempt.imperative: Verify TestSliverMergeExemptsSectorCuts proves BOTH: (1) a sliver away from a cut merges away, (2) a sliver whose boundary IS a sector line is preserved. Read _merge_slivers/_is_cut to confirm sector-cut boundaries are never removed. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4b-sliver-merge-exempt.finding: BLOCKING FINDING (independently reproduced, not just read from code). The two sliver-merge tests DO prove the exemption logic (away-from-cut merges; at-cut boundary survives) -- both pass, reproduced. But the underlying _merge_slivers TYPE-INHERITANCE is asymmetric between its two branches (src/physics/segment_map/derivation/sector_nesting.py:197-210), and this asymmetry is UNTESTED because every fixture in the suite happens to either take the forward branch, or (in the one backward-merge fixture, test_sliver_whose_boundary_is_a_sector_cut_is_preserved) has identical types on both sides of the merge (STRAIGHT/STRAIGHT), which masks the bug. FORWARD branch (line 201-202): 'del boundaries[i+1]; del types[i]' -- deletes the SLIVER's own type entry, so the surviving type is the NEIGHBOR's (i+1) -- matches its own comment ('absorb into the neighbor's type ... sliver's own type is the noise being removed'). BACKWARD branch (line 207-208): 'del boundaries[i]; del types[i-1]' -- deletes the LEFT NEIGHBOR's (i-1) type entry instead, so the surviving type is the SLIVER's OWN type -- the OPPOSITE of the forward branch and of the stated design intent. I independently reproduced this with a direct call (not from the test suite): nest_sectors on boundaries=[0,100,297.5,300,400,700,1000], types=[STRAIGHT,STRAIGHT,CORNER,STRAIGHT,STRAIGHT,CORNER], lines=[300.0,600.0] -- the 2.5m CORNER sliver [297.5,300) is blocked from forward-merging (300.0 is a sector cut) and merges BACKWARD, producing output types=[STRAIGHT,CORNER,STRAIGHT,STRAIGHT,STRAIGHT,CORNER] with boundaries=[0,100,300,400,600,700,1000] -- the ENTIRE [100,300) region is now CORNER, silently relabeling the real 197.5m STRAIGHT segment [100,297.5) as CORNER because a 2.5m numerical sliver happened to sit next to a sector cut. I confirmed the mirror (forward) case behaves correctly by symmetry: boundaries=[0,100,300,302.5,400,700,1000] same types, sliver [300,302.5) CORNER merges forward into [302.5,400) STRAIGHT -> correctly produces STRAIGHT, discarding the sliver. This is a genuine, reproducible correctness defect: silent mis-typing of a real segment (not the sliver) driven purely by which side of a sliver happens to be blocked by a sector cut -- exactly the 'plausible wrong output' the project's fail-visibly doctrine warns against, and it slipped past all 17 green tests because no fixture exercises a backward-merge with DIFFERING neighbor/sliver types. Fix candidate: line 208 should read 'del types[i]' (discard the sliver's own entry, keep the neighbor's), mirroring line 202 -- but this needs an explicit test with differing types on each side of a backward merge before it can be trusted.

consolidation.summary: G3 (issue #662, epic #659): nest_sectors/derive_sector_lines mostly meet the gate's charter -- split-not-snap is genuinely proven (exact-line insertion, flanking pieces keep the straddled segment's own type, pre-existing boundaries provably unperturbed), fail-closed is genuinely proven (5/5 bad-input cases raise SectorLineUnavailableError before any mutation), MIN_SEGMENT_LENGTH_M is imported with zero literal-5.0 shadowing, completeness and int8 sector assignment are correct, and derive_sector_lines is genuinely DB-only (zero fastf1 import; real 2023 Bahrain Q reproduction [1748.9001128850223, 3920.0948806410674] independently reproduced byte-for-byte).
